name: Amphetamine
drug_class: Central nervous system stimulant; monoamine releasing agent (phenethylamine)
route_note: Oral tablets, extended-release capsules, ODT or suspension; a dextroamphetamine transdermal system is approved in the US.
originator: Lazăr Edeleanu (first synthesis); Smith, Kline & French (first medical product)

first_approval.agency: AMA Council on Pharmacy and Chemistry

discovery.note: First synthesised as phenylisopropylamine; Gordon Alles independently resynthesised it in 1927 and characterised its stimulant effects.

tagline: Century-old stimulant that releases dopamine and noradrenaline; used for ADHD, narcolepsy
summary: Amphetamine is a CNS stimulant that releases dopamine and noradrenaline from nerve terminals. First marketed as the Benzedrine inhaler in the 1930s, it is now used, mainly as dextroamphetamine or mixed salts such as Adderall, for ADHD and narcolepsy. It is a Schedule II controlled substance because of its potential for misuse and addiction.
mechanism: Amphetamine enters monoamine neurons via the dopamine and noradrenaline transporters, disrupts vesicular storage by acting on VMAT2, and activates the intracellular receptor TAAR1. These actions cause the transporters to run in reverse, releasing dopamine and noradrenaline into the synapse, and also inhibit reuptake.

The dextro-enantiomer is more potent centrally, while the levo-enantiomer has relatively more peripheral noradrenergic activity. Increased catecholamine signalling in prefrontal and striatal circuits improves attention and wakefulness.
uses: Exogenous obesity (short-term, some amphetamine products in the US)

history.title: Synthesis
history.detail: Lazăr Edeleanu first synthesises amphetamine in Berlin.

history.title: Alles
history.detail: Gordon Alles resynthesises it and describes its sympathomimetic and stimulant effects.

history.title: Benzedrine inhaler
history.detail: Smith, Kline & French markets an over-the-counter amphetamine inhaler for nasal congestion.

history.title: Medical uses
history.detail: Amphetamine sulfate tablets are accepted for narcolepsy; Charles Bradley reports calming effects in children with behavioural problems.

history.title: Inhaler restricted
history.detail: The FDA makes Benzedrine inhalers prescription-only amid widespread misuse.

history.title: Schedule II
history.detail: Amphetamines are placed in Schedule II in the US and controlled internationally under the 1971 Convention on Psychotropic Substances.

history.title: Adderall
history.detail: Mixed amphetamine salts are marketed as Adderall for ADHD.

history.title: Adderall XR
history.detail: Once-daily extended-release mixed salts are approved.

history.title: Shortage
history.detail: The FDA announces a shortage of Adderall immediate-release tablets, which extends into 2023–2024.

pk.metabolism: Hepatic CYP2D6 hydroxylation and oxidative deamination
pk.excretion: Renal; unchanged fraction depends on urinary pH

serious: Sudden death and serious cardiovascular events in people with heart disease
safety.boxed_warning: High potential for abuse and misuse, which can lead to substance use disorder, including addiction; misuse and abuse can result in overdose and death. Assess risk before prescribing and monitor throughout treatment.

facts: Urinary acidification shortens and alkalinisation prolongs amphetamine's half-life.
Amphetamine was widely issued to military personnel during the Second World War.
